mainEntity.name: How long does it take to know if a dental implant has integrated successfully?

acceptedAnswer.text: Osseointegration generally takes between three and six months, though this varies depending on the individual's bone quality, overall health, and implant type. Dentists monitor progress through clinical checks and radiographic imaging. Some patients may require longer healing periods. Only a clinical assessment at each stage of treatment can confirm whether integration is progressing as expected. It is important not to place functional load on the implant until the dentist confirms that adequate stability has been achieved.

mainEntity.name: Can a dental implant feel stable but still have problems underneath?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it is possible for a patient to feel no obvious discomfort while issues such as early bone loss or soft tissue inflammation develop around an implant. This is one of the key reasons why routine professional monitoring, including radiographic assessment, is recommended even when the implant appears to be functioning well. Early detection of changes — before they become symptomatic — provides a better opportunity for effective management.

mainEntity.name: What causes a dental implant to become loose?

acceptedAnswer.text: An implant may feel loose due to several reasons, including insufficient osseointegration, peri-implantitis causing bone loss, damage to the abutment screw, or a loose crown rather than the implant itself. It is important to distinguish between a loose crown (restoration) and movement of the actual implant fixture, as these require different clinical responses. A professional assessment is essential to determine the cause and appropriate course of action. Attempting to adjust an implant without clinical guidance is not advisable.

mainEntity.name: Is resonance frequency analysis (RFA) available at all dental practices?

acceptedAnswer.text: RFA is not universally available across all dental practices. It is more commonly found in specialist implant clinics and practices that place a high volume of dental implants. Clinicians who do not have access to RFA can still assess implant stability effectively through clinical examination and digital radiography. If you would like to know whether a specific assessment tool is available at your clinic, it is worth asking during your consultation or review appointment.

mainEntity.name: Does smoking affect whether a dental implant stays secure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Smoking is a well-established risk factor for implant complications. It can impair blood circulation and tissue healing, reduce the effectiveness of the immune response, and increase the likelihood of peri-implant disease. Research suggests that implants placed in people who smoke have higher rates of complications compared with those placed in non-smokers. Patients who smoke and are considering dental implants are encouraged to discuss this openly with their dentist, as it forms part of the clinical suitability assessment. Support to reduce or stop smoking may be recommended.

mainEntity.name: How often should I attend for dental implant check-ups?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most dental clinicians recommend at least one annual review appointment specifically for implant monitoring, in addition to routine dental check-ups. Some patients — particularly those with a history of gum disease, those who smoke, or those who have had previous implant complications — may benefit from more frequent reviews. Your dentist will advise you on the monitoring schedule most appropriate for your individual circumstances.
